Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required wake-visual-signals skill to inspect the current multi-wake evidence before changing the policy. I’ll stay entirely within this Phase 2 workspace and won’t reconstruct the omitted research shelf.

The skill makes the evidence order explicit: anchor the images to observations and metrics, inspect the shared prewarm and rollout keyframes, then write the visual diagnosis before touching the candidate. I’m now inventorying the assigned guidance, sampled policies, and inherited optimizer notes so the single proposal is evidence-led.

The visual/metric comparison is now clear: the speed-gated damping rollout is the strongest current result, while every sampled rollout still reaches the target. The useful “failure” is therefore an optimization failure rather than a termination failure—the inherited static `0.75` posterior-share continuation—which deepened the return route. I’m checking that sheet directly before recording the new hypothesis.

The diagnosis is recorded before the policy edit, as required. The candidate will compose—but not extrapolate—the two independently positive bounded mechanisms: bearing-dependent posterior steering allocation and high-speed-only posterior damping, with all established gait, steering, and acceleration anchors unchanged.

The reusable guidance now records the new positive lesson: high-speed-localized damping improved every principal route/effort/load metric over the exact static anchor, but already showed slight anterior-speed transfer, so widening the gate is not justified. I’ll now run the mandated workspace checks and repair anything they flag; no CFD will be run.

The material-guidance and solver-boundary checks pass. The mandated Julia smoke check could not start because Julia is not installed in this environment; I’m doing the remaining static contract audit now, including exact `params.FIELD` ownership and the final three-file diff.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:44): composes the independently positive bearing-scheduled posterior share and speed-gated damping mechanisms.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records visual diagnosis, metrics, hypothesis, and falsification boundaries.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:118): materially revises the damping lesson using current rollout evidence.

Guidance materiality and solver-boundary checks passed. Static parameter ownership also passed. Julia was unavailable, so the lightweight runtime smoke check could not execute. No CFD was run.
